name: IL-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: Donna Miller's large fundraising and outside-spending advantage
Prediction markets price Democratic win near 97%
Open seat after Robin Kelly's retirement, but no competitive evidence
model.rationale: This Chicago-area seat leans heavily Democratic, and Miller has raised $2.4 million with over $4.4 million in outside support against a Republican with no reported fundraising. Markets price a Democratic win around 97%, consistent with the fundamentals-based margin of roughly 24 points.
model.watch: Any late polling showing the Republican within single digits, or a major outside-spending surge against Miller, would be the first sign of a real contest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Robin Kelly (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Democrats have held this South Side and south suburban Chicago district comfortably for years, and it carries an eighteen-point Democratic partisan lean. Robin Kelly's retirement to run for Senate leaves an open seat, but the Democratic nominee, Donna Miller, enters the general election with a decisive resource advantage: she has raised about $2.4 million and drawn more than $4.4 million in outside support, while Republican Michael Noack reports no fundraising on file.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and spending. Prediction markets put the Democratic win probability near 97%. The expected margin is roughly 24 points Democratic, with elevated uncertainty because polling is absent, but the seat remains firmly in the Safe Democratic column.
